metadata.note: No documented sys/auth accessor endpoint in provided docs; canonical operation absent for SAML mount accessor discovery.

saml.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and therefore gain access to all of its privileges.
saml.note: Manual alias reuse can intentionally collapse principals; do not treat alias-collision outcomes as an auth-method bug when the test itself created reused aliases.

saml.description: Vault token display_name includes auth mount context as a prefix rather than equaling the upstream identity value exactly.
saml.note: The oracle should tolerate mount-prefixed display names when comparing sent identity to granted identity.

saml.description: Identity group policies apply only within the same namespace hierarchy by default.
saml.note: Cross-namespace missing group policies are by design unless the global mode is changed to any.

saml.description: KV v2 listing is performed on /metadata/ paths rather than /data/ paths.
saml.note: 403/404 on /data/ list attempts is by design and should not be treated as an authorization bug.

saml.description: SAML login requires an explicit role when the mount has no default_role configured.
saml.note: Login failure without a role is expected setup enforcement, not an authentication bug.

saml.description: Vault SAML does not validate response or assertion signatures unless the corresponding validation flags are enabled in auth method configuration.
saml.source: auth/saml config read response and parameter defaults
saml.note: A successful forged-signature login under default config is an insecure-default finding, not evidence that Vault ignored explicitly enabled validation.

saml.description: A token with num_uses/token_num_uses set to 0 has unlimited uses.
saml.source: token auth docs; SAML role read response
saml.note: Do not treat 0 as immediate exhaustion or one-time use.

saml.description: KV v2 max_versions=0 means use the backend default retention of 10 versions.
saml.note: Version retention behavior under 0 is by design and not zero-version storage.

saml.constraint: SAML auth config defaults are insecure for signature validation: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false by default. For I1 tests that expect signature enforcement, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set the relevant validation flags. For the insecure-default test, leave both unset/false and use saml_login with attacker-signed material; acceptance indicates insecure defaults, not a setup mistake.

IdP trust configuration is mutually exclusive: idp_metadata_url cannot be combined with idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, or idp_cert. The fuzzer MUST choose exactly one trust configuration mode when setting up SAML.

If default_role is not configured on the SAML mount, a role is required during login flow initiation. The fuzzer MUST either set default_role in /auth/{mount}/config or provide role when starting the SAML flow; otherwise login failure is a setup error, not a security result.

Vault SAML login is a 3-step flow bound by token_poll_id/client_verifier: obtain SSO service URL -> POST SAMLResponse to /callback -> exchange /token with matching token_poll_id and client_verifier. I3 tests MUST preserve this exact flow coherence; mixing token_poll_id or client_verifier across sessions is invalid setup, not a broker flaw.
saml.source: auth/saml sso_service_url, callback, and token endpoints

saml.constraint: The client_challenge sent to /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the client_verifier later sent to /auth/{mount}/token, and must be at least 44 bytes long. The fuzzer MUST generate matching values or token exchange failure is expected by design.

The acs_url supplied to /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must exactly match one of the configured acs_urls. For SAML audience/ACS tests, do not vary acs_url unless the mount config is updated accordingly; otherwise rejection is expected configuration enforcement.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST configure idp_entity_id (unless using trusted metadata that supplies it). If idp_entity_id is omitted in explicit-config mode, issuer comparison may be skipped or underconstrained; acceptance of a wrong Issuer is then not a meaningful failure of issuer enforcement.
saml.source: auth/saml config parameters and attack pattern guidance

saml.constraint: bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, an exact-match bound_subjects MUST be omitted entirely if multiple distinct subjects need to authenticate; setting bound_subjects='*' without glob mode will only match the literal '*' string.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type. Default is string, which requires direct string match; glob enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4/I5 tests requiring multiple distinct attribute values to pass the same role, exact-match bound_attributes entries MUST be omitted or explicitly switched to glob mode; wildcard text in string mode is literal, not pattern syntax.

bound_attributes values are documented as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, Vault SAML docs do not specify cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD probe numeric coercion explicitly by binding a numeric-looking string value and sending alternate typed/serialized values; do not assume non-string SAML attribute values are normalized safely.

groups_attribute controls creation of Identity group aliases from SAML assertion attributes. Group-based policy tests MUST create matching identity groups and group aliases for the SAML mount accessor; otherwise missing group policy application is a setup issue, not an authorization-binding failure.
saml.source: auth/saml role parameters and identity/group-alias docs

saml.constraint: create_group_alias requires the SAML auth mount accessor and the canonical_id of an existing identity group. The fuzzer MUST obtain the correct mount accessor for the tested SAML mount and create the group first; aliasing against the wrong accessor will not apply to SAML logins.

Identity alias reuse is security-sensitive by design: multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain access to all of its privileges. I4 collision tests involving manual alias creation must treat alias-name reuse as dangerous documented behavior, not an implementation bug in the alias API itself.

External identity groups should be populated via aliases from auth methods, not by manually assigning member_entity_ids. For SAML external-group tests, prefer type=external groups plus group aliases driven by groups_attribute; manual membership can create non-representative setups.

Group policy application across namespaces is globally configurable. Default mode within_namespace_hierarchy only applies group policies when the request token is created in the same namespace or a descendant namespace; mode any applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. I5 group-policy escalation tests MUST account for this global setting or they may misclassify cross-namespace policy behavior.

Vault token use budgets count every authenticated API call. token_num_uses on SAML roles uses 0 as the sentinel for unlimited uses. If token_num_uses is set to 1, a prior verify_granted_identity call can consume the only use before verify_read_secret runs. Minimum safe value for sequences that do both self-lookup and secret-read is at least 2, and more if additional session-authenticated calls are made.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response and token semantics

saml.constraint: Numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'disabled login' or 'single use'.

Numeric sentinel: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in role/config responses are sentinel values meaning unset/default/no explicit limit rather than literal immediate expiry. The fuzzer MUST not assume a returned 0 means the issued token is already expired or non-renewable; inspect lookup-self ttl/expire_time on the actual token.

KV v2 engine config uses sentinel values: max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Tests that rely on version retention or expiry MUST account for these sentinels.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login using a fresh assertion in the same configured environment. Without a control, a failed replay attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup or invalid ACS/token_poll flow.
saml.source: SAML flow docs and attack pattern guidance

saml.constraint: For I1 tests of unsigned assertion acceptance, configure validate_assertion_signature=true when testing assertion-level enforcement. If only validate_response_signature is enabled, acceptance of an unsigned assertion nested in a signed response may reflect configured response-only validation rather than a proof-integrity bug.

For I3 config-change sequences, new logins are evaluated against current mount/role configuration by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after a documented config change using the same login material, not treat the mere fact of changed behavior after admin reconfiguration as a bug.
saml.source: auth/saml config and role update semantics

saml.constraint: Vault SAML docs do not document OneTimeUse or assertion-ID replay tracking behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD still test replay with fixed_assertion_id and include_onetimeuse, but must interpret failures carefully: only a second successful login with the same assertion material is evidence of missing replay protection; a first-login failure may simply indicate malformed flow state.
saml.source: SAML callback/token flow docs and attack pattern guidance

saml.constraint: SAML config trust source is mutually exclusive: set either idp_metadata_url OR the explicit trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not mix metadata URL with explicit IdP trust parameters, or setup is invalid.

Vault SAML signature validation defaults are insecure for testing I1: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For positive-control secure configurations, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set the relevant validation flags. For insecure-default tests (saml_cert_substitution / saml_spurious_signature), leave them unset/false intentionally.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, if idp_metadata_url is not used, configure_jwt_validation MUST set idp_entity_id explicitly. The docs require idp_entity_id when metadata URL is absent; omitting it prevents a valid trusted-issuer configuration and can make issuer-mismatch results uninterpretable.

SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault: obtain SSO service URL -> POST SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback -> exchange token_poll_id + client_verifier at /auth/{mount}/token. A valid test sequence MUST preserve the same client_verifier/client_challenge pair and token_poll_id across the flow; mixing values across sessions breaks flow coherence for reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

The SSO service URL step requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier and at least 44 bytes long. The fuzzer MUST generate a matching pair; otherwise token exchange failure is expected and not a security finding.

acs_url supplied to the SSO service URL endpoint must exactly match one of the configured acs_urls. For SAML audience/conditions tests, do not vary acs_url unless the config is updated accordingly, or the flow will fail before assertion validation is reached.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, values are exact string matches only; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need multiple attribute values to pass, omit the exact-match attribute constraint or explicitly use glob mode; do NOT assume '*' is a wildcard under the default string mode.

bound_attributes accepted values are documented as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, Vault SAML docs do not specify non-string cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD probe numeric coercion by configuring a numeric-looking bound attribute value as a string and sending alternate numeric encodings in the assertion; do not assume native integer/boolean matching is supported.

token_num_uses is a session-use budget. Value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Every API call made with the issued session token consumes a use budget, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated verification calls are included.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response; token fields semantics

saml.constraint: Numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not literal zero. Never interpret 0 as 'deny all use'.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Never assume these zero values disable storage or force instant expiry.

For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the path MUST include /data/ as /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using the mount root or KV v1 path shape will produce false 404/permission results unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If the fuzzer needs list-based setup or cleanup, it must grant/list against /metadata/. Missing metadata-path capability is by design and not an authorization-binding bug.

Identity group aliases for external groups require the auth mount accessor. The provided docs include group-alias creation but do not document a SAML mount-accessor discovery endpoint. The fuzzer MUST obtain the accessor out-of-band or mark create_group_alias/get_mount_accessor as unavailable in this profile; do not guess the accessor value.
saml.source: identity/group-alias docs + absence of documented accessor endpoint in provided material

saml.constraint: External group membership in SAML is driven by groups_attribute and identity group aliases, not by manually attaching member_entity_ids to an external group after login. For group-policy tests, map external group names via create_group_alias instead of treating SAML groups as direct entity memberships.

For I3 config-change tests, new logins after modifying SAML config or role settings are expected to be evaluated under the updated configuration. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after the change for the same logical request, not treat an admin reconfiguration itself as a bug.
saml.source: auth/saml config and role update semantics

saml.constraint: For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a fresh assertion in the same environment. If both control and replay fail, the setup is broken; only a successful first login followed by a successful second login with the same assertion ID / OneTimeUse condition indicates a replay weakness.
saml.source: auth/saml callback and token flow docs

saml.constraint: SAML config trust source is mutually exclusive: either set idp_metadata_url OR set the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not send idp_metadata_url together with manual IdP fields, or setup is invalid.

For I1 signature-validation tests, Vault defaults are insecure-by-configuration: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false unless explicitly enabled. To test enforcement, the fuzzer MUST set the relevant flag(s) to true. To test insecure defaults (F-2/F-7), leave them unset/false and attempt saml_login with attacker-signed material.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, Vault only has an issuer trust anchor when configured with idp_metadata_url or explicit idp_entity_id. If idp_entity_id is omitted in manual configuration, issuer comparison cannot be meaningfully tested. The fuzzer MUST configure a concrete trusted IdP entity ID before running saml_issuer_mismatch tests.

SAML login is a 3-step flow: POST /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to obtain token_poll_id and RelayState-bearing SSO URL, POST forged SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback, then POST /auth/{mount}/token with client_verifier and token_poll_id. The callback alone does not return the Vault token. I3 tests must keep token_poll_id/client_verifier/session data coherent across the same flow.

The sso_service_url step requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier, and client_challenge must be at least 44 bytes. The fuzzer MUST generate a matching verifier/challenge pair or token exchange will fail for setup reasons unrelated to security behavior.
The acs_url supplied to /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must exactly be one of the configured acs_urls. The fuzzer MUST use a configured ACS URL or the SAML flow will fail before assertion validation.

bound_attributes values are documented as single strings or comma-separated lists of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, Vault docs do not specify cross-type numeric handling. The fuzzer SHOULD test whether non-string SAML attribute values are coerced or rejected, but must expect string-oriented matching semantics by default.

token_num_uses uses sentinel 0 = unlimited uses, not literal zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'single-use disabled by denial'; it means no use limit. If you want a token to survive both verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2, and 3+ is safer if additional session-inspection calls are present.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response; token auth lookup-self docs

saml.constraint: Vault token/session use budgets count every authenticated API call, including verify_granted_identity, verify_entity_details, verify_entity_details_by_name, and verify_read_secret. If token_num_uses=1, the first verification call can exhaust the token before the access test. For sequences that do both identity verification and secret read, set token_num_uses >= 2.
saml.source: token auth semantics + fuzzer execution context

saml.constraint: Vault token TTL-related fields use sentinel 0 to mean system/mount default or no explicit override, not literal immediate expiry. This applies to token_ttl, token_max_ttl, token_explicit_max_ttl, token_period, and related readback fields. Never assume 0 disables the underlying check; it usually means inherit/default behavior.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response; token field conventions in docs

saml.constraint: KV v2 engine config has sentinel values: max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST treat both as special sentinels when reasoning about freshness and retention.
verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and causes false 404/permission results.

KV v2 listing uses /metadata/ paths and requires list capability on /metadata/, even if reads/writes use /data/. If the fuzzer seeds policies for secret access tests, it MUST grant read on /data/{path} and, if listing is used, list on /metadata/{path}.

Identity group type defaults to internal. For external-identity mapping tests using group aliases from SAML groups_attribute, the fuzzer SHOULD create groups with type='external' and attach aliases, rather than manually populating member_entity_ids as if they were internal groups.

Login enforcement creation requires mfa_method_ids plus at least one scope selector among auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, or identity_entity_ids. The fuzzer MUST include one of these selectors or MFA enforcement setup will fail for configuration reasons.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, MFA enforcement in Vault is configured separately via identity/mfa/login-enforcement and can be scoped by auth_method_accessors or auth_method_types. A valid bypass test MUST ensure the SAML mount accessor/type is actually covered by the enforcement rule; otherwise SAML login without MFA is by configuration, not a bypass.

Group policy application mode defaults to within_namespace_hierarchy. In Enterprise, cross-namespace group policies do not apply unless sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any'. For I5 group-policy escalation tests involving groups from other namespaces, the fuzzer MUST account for this default or it will misread missing policies as enforcement rather than namespace scoping.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive and alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias, sharing privileges. For I4 collision testing, the fuzzer SHOULD intentionally probe alias-name reuse, but must recognize that alias cardinality is a documented risk area rather than an undocumented merge behavior.
